subject.title: Plugin SDK: add native registerMcpServer for managed MCP

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-managed MCP server registration as a public Plugin SDK contract for dynamic capability inventories, and under what stdio process-launching boundary?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding this API changes the public plugin contract and lets plugins ask OpenClaw to launch MCP server subprocesses, so automation should not choose the security/product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow SDK design
options.body: Proceed only with a maintainer-approved design for stdio-only registration, validation, precedence, workspace scoping, lifecycle cleanup, operator visibility, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep bundle/config MCP only
options.body: Close or defer the native SDK API and direct plugin authors to bundle MCP, `mcp.servers`, or ClawHub until a stronger product/security gap is proven.

options.title: Request an RFC first
options.body: Ask for a short design RFC comparing bundle/config MCP, dynamic plugin lifecycle needs, and security controls before implementation resumes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow SDK design
recommendation.body: Proceed only with a maintainer-approved design for stdio-only registration, validation, precedence, workspace scoping, lifecycle cleanup, operator visibility, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of Plugin SDK/API builder and MCP operator/runtime seams, which are the central decision surfaces for this API.
